result: Hardening fixes address the prior major gaps: Source-RCON now validates authentication response id/type/body, validates command response id/type, rejects common command-error bodies, and mutation endpoints no longer falsely report those errors as success. Viewer persistent-list mutation controls are hidden/disabled, polling cleanup remains correct, and prior guards/rate limits/CSRF/audit integration remain present. Tests/build pass. Remaining gaps: RconEndpoint is still assigned before process.Start and is not cleared if startup throws; connection/refusal IOException is not translated to the documented 503 unavailable response; and no focused packet/auth/error fixture tests exist, so live transport behavior remains static-only verified.

evidence.outcome: Passed; Vite production build completed with existing SignalR Rollup annotation warnings.
Auth packet requires id=1/type=2/empty body; command packet requires id=2/type=0; common error response bodies throw InvalidOperationException.
RCON invalid-operation/timeout map to 503; running guard maps 409 and validation maps 400.
Loopback ephemeral endpoint and random password are generated before process.Start; stop/exit clear endpoint, but startup exceptions before lifecycle cleanup can leave stale endpoint state.
canMutate is owner/admin only; viewer live and persistent-list mutations are hidden; polling clears on unmount; live mutations require confirmations.
Authenticated API group retains CSRF and mutation audit behavior; live mutations retain 20-per-minute rate limiting.

next_slice.summary: Clear RconEndpoint in startup exception/finally path, map IOException/SocketException to 503, and add Source-RCON packet fixture tests covering auth failure, mismatched IDs/types, command errors, timeout, and framing.

blockers: Startup exception can leave an in-memory RconEndpoint; socket/IO failures can escape endpoint handlers as 500 instead of 503 instead of 503.
